1.1.title: Write docs/hearth-reporting-pipeline-v1.md (end-to-end reporting spec)
1.1.description: Create a new doc that de-black-boxes the reporting pipeline end to end. Read src/lib/report/coverage.ts, src/lib/report/deterministic-coverage.ts, src/lib/report/coverage-narrative.ts, src/app/api/report/export/route.ts, src/lib/ai/annotation-draft.ts, and src/config/jurisdictions.ts first. Document: (1) surfaces (report + portfolio pages, all /api/report* routes); (2) the DB tables (complianceReports, workSamples, workSampleAnnotations, learnerDloStatus, observationDloLinks); (3) coverage resolution with the EXACT gates from coverage.ts getDeterministicCoverage — explicit non-blank state gate (coverage.ts:68) then frameworkHasMappings gate, else {mode:'fallback'}; (4) the two runtime AI touchpoints (annotation drafts, progression summaries) with their edit-protection safeguards, and confirm no read-time LLM in coverage; (5) PDF structure per tier — cd_level (QLD/SA/NT) vs learning_area (NSW/VIC/WA/TAS/ACT); (6) a 'Coverage fallback recovery' runbook section: how a blank-state family activates deterministic coverage (set state -> framework must have authored mappings -> snapshot rebuild). ALSO add two rows to the CLAUDE.md reference table: one for this doc and one for docs/hearth-constellation-architecture-v1.md (created by task 1.3). This task is the SOLE owner of CLAUDE.md edits in this plan.
1.1.done_when: docs/hearth-reporting-pipeline-v1.md exists and grep finds sections for coverage resolution, fallback recovery, and PDF tiers; CLAUDE.md reference table contains rows for both hearth-reporting-pipeline-v1.md and hearth-constellation-architecture-v1.md
1.1.contracts: Deterministic gate order (from src/lib/report/coverage.ts): (1) if state is null/blank -> {mode:'fallback'}; (2) frameworkKeyForState(state); (3) if no DLO doc has a regulatoryMapping with that frameworkKey -> {mode:'fallback'}; (4) else rollupCoverage + deriveCoverageSignals -> {mode:'deterministic'}. Only developing(0.5)/demonstrating(1.0) DLO tiers contribute; emerging/not-started = 0.

2.2.title: Surface silent DLO-confirm background-refetch failure as a retryable notice
2.2.description: In src/app/(auth)/our-story/capabilities/page.tsx (background refetch around lines 79-122), a failed post-confirm snapshot refetch is currently silent — the parent keeps a stale-but-real view and never learns the rebuild may not have persisted. Extend the R26 trust contract ('a failed load must never read as success/empty') to this path: when the background refetch after a DLO confirm fails, surface a gentle, retryable inline notice (e.g. 'We couldn't refresh — tap to retry') without discarding the current view. Keep copy warm and non-alarming per the parent-journey Stage 2/3 contract. Add/extend page.test.tsx to cover the failed-refetch-shows-notice-and-retry case. This task OWNS page.tsx and page.test.tsx.

2.2.contracts: Do not regress the existing R26 load-failure states (three cases already in page.test.tsx). Run tests on node@24. Reduced-motion + warm copy per hearth-parent-journey-v1.md.

3.1.title: Work-sample orphan integrity when an assigned entry is deleted
3.1.description: A learning entry can be assigned to a workSamples slot (workSamples.entryId FK). Verify what happens today when that entry is deleted: locate the entry-delete API route (search src/app/api/entries for the DELETE handler), and trace whether it clears or blocks slots referencing the entry. If deletion orphans the slot (entryId points to a now-missing entry -> PDF renders '—', slot still shows 'selected'), add a guard: either block deletion while the entry is assigned to a slot (return a clear 409 telling the parent to remove it from the report first) OR clear the slot on delete — pick whichever matches existing cascade conventions in schema.ts and note the choice in the PR. Add a regression integration test (real Postgres per test-pilot-runbook.md) proving the chosen behaviour.
3.1.done_when: deleting an entry assigned to a work-sample slot no longer silently orphans the slot (blocked with 409 or slot cleared); a new integration test asserts the behaviour and passes via `npm run test:integration:local`
3.1.contracts: Verify the actual delete-route path first (the [entryId] segment name may differ, e.g. [id]); update files accordingly. Follow existing FK cascade style in src/lib/db/schema.ts. Integration tests use transaction-rollback isolation and real pgvector Postgres.
